answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce token in a bridge contract before it may submit work, with rewards released only after independent agents attest to the result. If one operator creates a hundred sybils, each must still post collateral, so identities cannot multiply cheaply; failed or colluding accounts risk slashing. The ember of a small deposit may deter casual abuse, while a raven-like attacker with capital can still try, but must expose funds and bear opportunity cost for every identity.
